obligations.note: release() now returns the stored release only if it is less than one day old. A replay of the same instruction_id after 24 hours still passes the approval and payee checks and calls _send_disbursement again, so a second disbursement goes to core banking before add_release runs.

Ledger entry ACR-0403, the sample trace for PAY-2, covers payments.py#release, whose behaviour this change alters, so it has lapsed. No valid replacement evidence establishes PAY-2, and the new code violates it.

Ticket CHG-26637 is a standard ticket, approved on 2026-10-03 by Erik Brandt (change_manager) before the change opened. Its component payments.payments covers the only touched path, apps/baseline-payments/payments/payments.py.
Mara Costa (change_approver for payments) gave a code_review approval. She is a different person from the author, Sofia Santos.
The approval names head commit a2985128, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json reports success on head a2985128, and the registered PAY-2/PAY-1/MC-1 control tests are listed as passing. However, the JUnit report is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time, from host dev-laptop-7.local rather than ci-runner-08, so it cannot be tied to this commit's CI run.
The only touched component is payments.payments, which is not marked security_sensitive, so no security_review approval is required.
No exception is invoked, and none in the register covers PAY-2 or payments.payments. The PAY-2 deviation is therefore unexcused.

summary: The change limits replay protection in release() to a one-day window. Releasing the same payment instruction again after 24 hours would send a second disbursement, which directly violates PAY-2. The prior PAY-2 evidence has lapsed under LAP-1, and no exception covers the deviation. The CI report's provenance is also inconsistent with the recorded run. The ticket and approval records are otherwise in order, but the PAY-2 violation requires rejection.
